questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

On the ball

options.text: To be very excited or joyful

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"On the ball"** means to be **very alert and aware of what is happening**. (सजग और जागरूक होना)

 
 
• **Example:** The new manager is really **on the ball **and has already made several positive changes.
 
 
 
• **"Alert and aware about something"** means being attentive and conscious about the situation around you. (सतर्क और जागरूक होना)
 
 
• **Example:** You need to be **alert and aware about your surroundings** when you are traveling alone.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To be very excited or joyful **(बहुत उत्साहित या आनंदित होना): Feeling a high level of excitement or happiness.

 
 
• **Example:** She was very excited and joyful when she received the news of her promotion.
 
 
 
• **On a new journey **(एक नई यात्रा पर): Starting a new phase or experience in life.
 
 
• **Example:** He is on a new journey to self-discovery after quitting his job.
 
 
 
• **On the contrary** (इसके विपरीत): Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with a previous statement.
 
 
• **Example:** I thought the test would be hard; on the contrary, it was quite easy.

An ant can carry up to 50 __times it's__ body weight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of **"it's" instead of "its".**
 
• **"It's"** is a contraction for **"it is"** or** "it has," whereas "its" **is a possessive pronoun.
 
• The correct phrase should be **"times its,"** ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"An ant can carry up to 50 times** its** body weight."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the adjective "**hardest**" instead of the adverb "**hard**."
 
• Adjectives describe nouns, while **adverbs describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs**. In this context, **"study"** is a** verb** and should be modified by an adverb.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**to study hard**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 1** of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Sham is trying to study **hard **for his upcoming exams."*

• **Option 4: "his upcoming exams"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
